transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

It is unlikely that the motor is failing given the appliance is only four months old and still under guarantee. The symptoms described are more likely caused by a blockage or a sensor issue triggering the automatic power adjustment. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the motor or electronics inside. Clogged filters make the motor work harder and run the battery down faster. Wash them in cold water and let them dry fully (24 hours). Were the filters clogged (and are they clean now), or were they clean already?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

The filters were clean already, I washed the one at the back last month and left it to dry for a day. I should mention there's no heat, no burning smell and no warning lights, but the motor noise still changes between the tiles and the rug.

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Detach the wand and floorhead and look through each part, and check the bin inlet — a coin dropped through the wand should fall straight out. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is a hose split, or was it all clear?

I looked down the wand and it's clear, nothing stuck in it. I haven't taken the head apart though, and I won't open the motor body or undo any screws as it's under guarantee. Is there anything else you'd like me to check?

No, there is nothing further for you to check. Since the vacuum is only four months old and still under guarantee, you should contact Dyson support directly for a repair or replacement. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
